program.source: export function evaluate({ inputs, time }) { const launchSpeed = inputs.launchSpeed; const gravity = 9.8; const t = time; const height = launchSpeed * t - 0.5 * gravity * t * t; const velocity = launchSpeed - gravity * t; const apexTime = launchSpeed / gravity; const apexHeight = (launchSpeed * launchSpeed) / (2 * gravity); const scaleY = 40; const baseY = 360; const ballY = baseY - height * scaleY; const ballX = 320; let motionState = "Moving up"; if (Math.abs(velocity) < 0.05) { motionState = "Still for an instant"; } else if (velocity < 0) { motionState = "Moving down"; } const gravityState = "Gravity pulls down"; const objects = []; objects.push(sdk.panel({ x: 40, y: 40, w: 560, h: 360, title: "Vertical Toss", state: motionState })); objects.push(sdk.axis("heightAxis", { x: 100, y: 360, length: 280, orientation: "y", min: 0, max: 2.5, ticks: [0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5], label: "Height", unit: "m" })); objects.push(sdk.groundMark("ground", ballX, baseY, 60, "Launch")); objects.push(sdk.circle("ball.toss", ballX, ballY, 24, { role: "output" })); if (Math.abs(velocity) >= 0.05) { const vDir = velocity > 0 ? "up" : "down"; objects.push(sdk.vector("vec.v", { x: ballX + 20, y: ballY }, { value: Math.abs(velocity), direction: vDir }, { scale: 8, label: "v", role: "observed" })); } objects.push(sdk.vector("vec.a", { x: ballX - 25, y: ballY }, { value: gravity, direction: "down" }, { scale: 4, label: "a", role: "warning" })); const calloutLines = [motionState, "Gravity pulls down"]; objects.push(sdk.callout(ballX + 45, ballY - 20, calloutLines, { id: "callout.toss", role: "output" })); const readouts = [{ id: "motionState", value: motionState }, { id: "gravityState", value: gravityState }]; return { frame: { width: 640, height: 420, objects, readouts }, quantities: { launchSpeed, gravity, apexTime, apexHeight, velocity, height } }; }

manifest.title: The ball stops rising. Gravity doesn’t stop.
manifest.summary: Gravity slows the ball on the way up and speeds it up on the way down. At the top, the ball is still for an instant while gravity pulls it downward.
manifest.description: A vertical height scale shows a ball tossed upwards. A blue arrow indicates velocity, shortening as the ball rises and pointing downward as it falls. A dashed warm gravity arrow remains constant throughout.
manifest.instructions: Change launch speed, then press Play. At the top, playback pauses so you can inspect the arrows.
